footnotes: Superseded: this run is not in the published table; the run measured on 2026-11-12/13 (`data/2026/cycle-1/monitorable.*`) replaces it. The unit was charged 15.8 MB of disk writes between 17 minutes and 7.8 hours after the install (14.5 MB per 24 h in the idle window) and nothing after. Checks on the bed's boxes on 2026-11-12 showed the mechanism: ext4 writes its metadata through the block device's inode, 2 to 2.7 MB per hour on an idle box, and the kernel charges all writeback of one inode to a single cgroup, whichever owns it. That this unit's cgroup owned it for those hours is inferred from the matching rate and write sizes, because the box had been rebuilt before the check; the agent's page cache stayed at 28,672 bytes for the whole run and its on-disk footprint at the end equals run 2's. `docs/RUN-2026-slot5.md` has the evidence and the rule under which the run was replaced. The footnote this run carried while it was published follows.

Run 1 (box-1): this run's 14.5 MB of disk writes all fall in the first 7.8 hours after the install and then stop; in that span the agent logged nothing, its on-disk footprint did not grow, and its CPU, memory and network figures are the same as in the hours after. The same writes (the same hourly rate and block sizes, about 16 MB in all) appear in one run of another agent on another box and day (Beszel, run 3) and in neither agent's other two runs, so they are most likely the box's filesystem writeback charged to this unit's cgroup, not the agent's own writes. The cause is not established; the figure is published as measured.
